A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same PLOT research work. Their complete main texts, equations, tables, figures, and appendices are readable and support comparison. Changed experimental conditions limit direct performance comparisons, not comparison of the documents.

before.justification: V1 reports original KITTI pseudo-label evaluations, detector-training results, component ablations, runtime measurements, and qualitative experiments, including appendix analyses.

after.justification: V2 reports original results on KITTI, KITTI-360, and Waymo, alongside component ablations, noise experiments, and qualitative video analyses in the main text and appendix.

M1.justification: V1 uses object-mask matching, object-level registration, label recovery, and PCA orientation estimation. V2 adds background-based camera-motion estimation, motion-based orientation for dynamic objects, ego-motion correction, and Global Object Memory with persistent entries, refinement, and merging. These substantially extend the inference procedure beyond v1's local association and recovery rules.

E1.justification: V2 adds quantitative training and evaluation on KITTI-360 and Waymo, including continuous sequences and adverse driving conditions, beyond v1's KITTI quantitative evaluation. Appendix A2.3 also adds GMOT-40 to the reported qualitative coverage. MOT17, DIVOTrack, Pexels, and MOSE were already represented in v1.

E2.justification: The KITTI car comparison expands from v1 Table 2 to include DEVIANT, OVMono3D, 3D-MOOD, WeakMono3D, SKD-WM3D, and MonoSOWA in v2 Table 1. WeakMono3D and SKD-WM3D were discussed in v1 but lacked corresponding table results. In qualitative comparisons, 3D-MOOD replaces Cube R-CNN; OVM3D-Det remains.

E3.justification: V2 introduces longer tracking windows and protocols for additional benchmarks. Its raw-label evaluation changes from KITTI training data to validation data with static/all-object subsets. Crucially, baseline scores described as IoU 0.5 in v1 Section 4.1/Table 2 reappear under IoU 0.3 in v2 Table 1, alongside separate 0.5 results. This establishes revised reported settings, not that every experiment was rerun.

E4.justification: V2 adds memory ablations, raw-label versus trained-detector comparisons, camera-motion ablations, and controlled tracker/depth-noise experiments, including rigid versus similarity alignment. It revises existing frame-count and estimated-intrinsics analyses and expands association failure cases. V1's separate depth-clipping and uniform-scale-factor ablations disappear. Appendix A3 inconsistently identifies the noise experiment as KITTI versus a sampled Waymo scene.

E5.justification: Neither version reports experimental seed counts, repeated-run variability, confidence intervals, or significance tests. V2's controlled noise perturbations are robustness experiments, not newly introduced statistical uncertainty reporting.

E6.justification: V2 adds substantial benchmark and ablation results and replaces the earlier raw-label result breakdown. For example, Table 6 newly reports KITTI-360 Easy AP3D at IoU 0.3 of 48.14 without memory and 54.78 with memory. Runtime results also change substantially. These additions and replacements cannot generally be interpreted as same-setting improvements over v1 because configurations and reported protocols differ.

T1.justification: The Hungarian matching and Procrustes foundations remain. V2 extends the mathematical description with background-motion estimation, world-coordinate trajectories, and dynamic/static orientation equations. V1's explicit depth-clipping, height-prior scaling, and center-estimation formulas are omitted. These revise the applied geometric formulation; neither version introduces theorems or proofs.

C1.justification: The shared claim of training-free video-based 3D labeling remains, but v2 makes camera/object motion reasoning and persistent identity consistency through Global Object Memory central contributions. V1 instead emphasizes the first tracking-based aggregation approach and shape-based attribute estimation. V2's conclusion additionally proposes applicability to CAD retrieval and object reconstruction.

C2.justification: V2 adds substantive explanations linking memory to identity consistency, detector training to regularization of noisy labels, and temporal depth-scale fluctuations to degradation in box accuracy. It adds limitations concerning static-object orientation and tracking-window boundaries. Limited viewpoint variation, clutter, and depth dependence were already discussed in v1; their recurrence alone is not new.

D1.justification: V2 documents AllTracker instead of CoTracker3, MoGe2 instead of DepthPro for in-the-wild videos, tracking thresholds, window handling, hardware, and additional dataset splits. It adds a project-page pointer and states that partial source code accompanies the supplement; availability cannot be verified from the PDFs. Conversely, v1's explicit size/center construction and detailed pseudo-label matching and metric definitions are no longer supplied.

R1.justification: V2 substantially repositions PLOT against temporal pseudo-labeling and tracking-based 3D perception, particularly MonoSOWA, ViPE, and Vid2CAD, and adds newer open-set and reconstruction literature. The related-work structure changes from emphasizing zero-shot perception foundations to distinguishing object-level temporal reasoning from competing approaches. This goes beyond citation renumbering or publication updates.

P1.justification: The abstract, introduction, related work, method narrative, and experimental discussion are extensively rewritten. The introduction replaces the contribution list with a two-challenge narrative, experiments prioritize benchmark detection, and the appendix is reorganized into method details, settings, analyses, failures, and qualitative results. References move after the supplement, and the title and affiliations change.

P2.justification: V2 changes the document from two columns to one, redraws the architecture illustration, adds a memory flowchart, and substantially rebuilds comparison and ablation tables. It introduces new temporal-consistency, failure, and benchmark visualizations while replacing or regrouping earlier qualitative panels. These are extensive display changes beyond pagination and numerical updates.

improvement.justification: V2 strengthens v1's limited quantitative validation through KITTI-360 and Waymo experiments, direct temporal/open-set comparisons, and targeted memory, motion, and noise ablations. These improve the evidence for the proposed mechanisms and applicability. The net gain is tempered by omitted box-construction and metric details, unexplained reassignment of earlier scores to a different IoU threshold, and contradictory dataset descriptions in Appendix A3. Thus, the broader evidence supports improvement, but the documentation regressions limit its overall extent.
